channel.description: Video essays about design, branding, identity, and culture. Why things look the way they do — and what that means.
channel.itunes:author: The Threads of Culture

item.title: Why Every Brand Looks the Same Now (The Design Crisis No One Admits)
item.description:
You've noticed it. Every logo is black, sans-serif, and stripped of personality — from luxury fashion to toothpaste startups. But this isn't just a trend. It's a full-blown design crisis, and it's erasing the visual identity of entire industries.
In this video essay, we trace the origins of branding's sameness epidemic back to the 2010s, exploring how minimalism went from a principled design philosophy to a corporate safety blanket. We look at the forces driving the convergence — from Silicon Valley's influence on visual culture to the constraints of digital-first design to the creeping fear of standing out in a market obsessed with appearing "clean" and "modern."
But this isn't just a story about what went wrong. We also spotlight the brands, designers, and creative directors who are pushing back — embracing maximalism, weirdness, heritage typography, and visual identities that actually dare to be memorable. From indie brands to legacy houses rediscovering their roots, there's a quiet rebellion brewing against the beige blur of modern branding.
Whether you're a designer, a marketer, a brand strategist, or just someone who's wondered why your entire Instagram feed looks like it was designed by the same person — this one's for you.
If this made you think differently about the brands around you, subscribe for more essays on design, culture, and the invisible forces shaping how we see the world.
